My memory doesn't hold the owner's exact words from those CI complaints on 10-15, so I can't quote what he objected to.

What I do have are the standing rules that came out of that period:
- "Never cut tests/delegates unasked" was the lesson I carried forward. So no, I may not cancel or cut tests to speed things up unless he asks.
- I may skip useless tests and repeated runs that follow no code change. Real tests stay.
- Speed gains have to come from root fixes, such as running a check once per tree, the gate skipping a redundant Apple compile, and a warm gate build root.

If you need his actual objection, it's in the earlier conversation, which I can't see.
